165:             import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
166: 
167:             fig = plt.gcf()
168: 
169:         if not fig.get_axes():
170:             new_axes = True
171:         ax = fig.gca()
172: 
173:     # Create a storage bucket for this axes in case we need it
174:     if ax not in __AXMAP:
175:         __AXMAP[ax] = dict()
176: 
177:     return ax, new_axes
178: 
179: 
180: def segments(
181:     intervals,
182:     labels,
183:     base=None,
184:     height=None,
185:     text=False,
186:     text_kw=None,
187:     ax=None,
188:     prop_cycle=None,
189:     **kwargs,
190: ):
191:     """Plot a segmentation as a set of disjoint rectangles.
192: 
193:     Parameters
194:     ----------
195:     intervals : np.ndarray, shape=(n, 2)
196:         segment intervals, in the format returned by
197:         :func:`mir_eval.io.load_intervals` or
198:         :func:`mir_eval.io.load_labeled_intervals`.
199:     labels : list, shape=(n,)
200:         reference segment labels, in the format returned by
201:         :func:`mir_eval.io.load_labeled_intervals`.
202:     base : number
203:         The vertical position of the base of the rectangles.
204:         By default, this will be the bottom of the plot.
205:     height : number
206:         The height of the rectangles.
207:         By default, this will be the top of the plot (minus ``base``).
208:         .. note:: If either `base` or `height` are provided, both must be provided.
209:     text : bool
210:         If true, each segment's label is displayed in its
211:         upper-left corner
212:     text_kw : dict
213:         If ``text == True``, the properties of the text
214:         object can be specified here.
215:         See ``matplotlib.pyplot.Text`` for valid parameters
216:     ax : matplotlib.pyplot.axes
217:         An axis handle on which to draw the segmentation.
218:         If none is provided, a new set of axes is created.
219:     prop_cycle : cycle.Cycler
220:         An optional property cycle object to specify style properties.
221:         If not provided, the default property cycler will be retrieved from matplotlib.
222:     **kwargs
223:         Additional keyword arguments to pass to
224:         ``matplotlib.patches.Rectangle``.
225: 
226:     Returns
227:     -------
228:     ax : matplotlib.pyplot.axes._subplots.AxesSubplot
229:         A handle to the (possibly constructed) plot axes
230:     """
231:     if text_kw is None:
232:         text_kw = dict()
233:     text_kw.setdefault("va", "top")
234:     text_kw.setdefault("clip_on", True)
235:     text_kw.setdefault("bbox", dict(boxstyle="round", facecolor="white"))
236: 
237:     # Make sure we have a numpy array
238:     intervals = np.atleast_2d(intervals)
239: 
240:     seg_def_style = dict(linewidth=1)
241: 
242:     ax, new_axes = __get_axes(ax=ax)
243: 
244:     if prop_cycle is None:
245:         __AXMAP[ax].setdefault("prop_cycle", mpl.rcParams["axes.prop_cycle"])
246:         __AXMAP[ax].setdefault("prop_iter", iter(mpl.rcParams["axes.prop_cycle"]))
247:     elif "prop_iter" not in __AXMAP[ax]:
248:         __AXMAP[ax]["prop_cycle"] = prop_cycle
249:         __AXMAP[ax]["prop_iter"] = iter(prop_cycle)
250: 
251:     prop_cycle = __AXMAP[ax]["prop_cycle"]
252:     prop_iter = __AXMAP[ax]["prop_iter"]
253: 
254:     if new_axes:
255:         ax.set_yticks([])
256: 
257:     if base is None and height is None:
258:         # If neither are provided, we'll use axes coordinates to span the figure
259:         base, height = 0, 1
260:         transform = ax.get_xaxis_transform()
261: 
262:     elif base is not None and height is not None:
263:         # If both are provided, we'll use data coordinates
264:         transform = None
265:     else:
266:         raise ValueError("When specifying base or height, both must be provided.")
267: 
268:     seg_map = dict()
269: 
270:     for lab in labels:
271:         if lab in seg_map:
272:             continue
273: 
274:         try:
275:             properties = next(prop_iter)
276:         except StopIteration:
277:             prop_iter = iter(prop_cycle)
278:             __AXMAP[ax]["prop_iter"] = prop_iter
279:             properties = next(prop_iter)
280: 
281:         style = {
282:             k: v
283:             for k, v in properties.items()
284:             if k in ["color", "facecolor", "edgecolor", "linewidth"]
285:         }
286:         # Swap color -> facecolor here so we preserve edgecolor on rects
287:         style.setdefault("facecolor", style["color"])
288:         style.pop("color", None)
289:         seg_map[lab] = seg_def_style.copy()
290:         seg_map[lab].update(style)
291:         seg_map[lab].update(kwargs)
292:         seg_map[lab]["label"] = lab
293: 
294:     for ival, lab in zip(intervals, labels):
295:         rect = ax.axvspan(ival[0], ival[1], ymin=base, ymax=height, **seg_map[lab])
296:         seg_map[lab].pop("label", None)
297: 
298:         if text:
299:             ann = ax.annotate(
300:                 lab,
301:                 xy=(ival[0], height),
302:                 xycoords=transform,
303:                 xytext=(8, -10),
304:                 textcoords="offset points",
305:                 **text_kw,
306:             )
307:             ann.set_clip_path(rect)
308: 
309:     return ax
310: 
311: 
312: def labeled_intervals(
313:     intervals,
314:     labels,
315:     label_set=None,
316:     base=None,
317:     height=None,
318:     extend_labels=True,
319:     ax=None,
320:     tick=True,
